<!--
===============================================================================
WHAT THIS DOCUMENT DOES  (read this before running)
===============================================================================
This is the DEMAND-SIDE script of the CBA -> employment pipeline. It turns the
cost-benefit (CBA) output into signed GLORIA-product demand vectors, then
multiplies them by the pre-computed employment matrix L to get domestic jobs.

It replaces the old "$1M-per-strategy" scaffold
("Sisepuede - Transformation demand vectors for GLORIA.Rmd"). Three upgrades:

  1. VALUES ARE CBA DOLLARS, NOT $1M. Each transformation's demand is
     multiplier x delta(physical quantity between scenario and BAU runs),
     split into a COST stream (+) and a SAVINGS stream (-). See Section 4.
  2. JOBS COME FROM THE L MATRIX, NOT FROM RE-RUNNING MINDSET. We built L once
     in Python (EXTRACT_L_MATRIX.py). Here we just do jobs = L %*% f in R.
     L already encodes the Leontief inverse, 2019 employment coefficients, and
     the import-origin split; it returns DOMESTIC jobs only. See Section 6.
  3. ELECTRICITY MIX IS DYNAMIC & SCENARIO-BASED (per-year), not the static
     2019 IEA mix used in the old code. See Section 3. (Optional; see flags.)

DESIGN CHOICE (agreed): the cost structure is treated as a BILL OF MATERIALS in
FINAL-DEMAND space -- "$x is spent buying product g" -- and L was built to match
that. We do NOT route it through MINDSET's capital-formation converter (that
step is for "who invests" vectors and would double-process a bill of materials).

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PIPELINE MAP (which section produces what)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  S1  Setup + paths ....................... libraries, file locations
  S2  Cost structures (Eora26 x strategy) .. the sector weights per transformation
  S3  Dynamic electricity mix [OPTIONAL] ... per-year grid composition (scenario)
  S4  CBA dollar scaling .................... multiplier x delta -> signed $ per strategy
  S5  Eora26 -> GLORIA (120 products) ....... spread each sector weight to products
  S6  Employment ........................... jobs = L %*% f  (domestic)
  S7  Export + diagnostics

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
FILES STILL NEEDED FROM FERNANDO  (script runs without them; sections skip)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  [PENDING-1] COST-STRUCTURE MASTER. Two candidates exist on disk:
        (a) Data/.../ATTRIBUTE_STRATEGY_transformations_vectors.xlsx  (spine-native, OLD)
        (b) Data/Cost Structure/Transformations - Cost Structure vectors (SSP CBA).xlsx (NEW, 18 sheets)
      Set COST_MASTER below to whichever is authoritative. Default = (a).
  [PENDING-2] STRATEGY RE-KEY CROSSWALK: Fernando's finished
        old strategy_id  <->  new strategy_code / output_variable_name  map.
      Set REKEY_FILE + its key columns in S4 when ready. Until then, S4 joins
      the CBA lines to strategies on the subsector token as a STOPGAP and flags it.

Everything else needed already exists (paths verified 2026-07-25):
  - L matrix .................. MINDSET_module-main/SSP - Results/L_matrix_MAR.csv

```{r setup, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readxl)
library(openxlsx)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

# S1. Setup and file locations

All inputs live INSIDE the `SSP-employment_estimates` repo, so anyone who syncs
that repo can run this file — regardless of the folder they store it in. The repo
root is auto-detected from the Rmd's own location; no per-machine edit needed.

```{r paths}
# ---- Repo root (auto-detected) ---------------------------------------------
# This Rmd lives in  <SSP-employment_estimates>/Codes/ , so the repo root is the
# parent of the Codes/ folder. knitr sets the working dir to the Rmd's dir; when
# run interactively we fall back to walking up from getwd() until we find the repo
# marker. NO hard-coded absolute path -> portable across collaborators' machines.
find_repo_root <- function() {
  # 1) knitr: directory of the Rmd being knit.
  d <- tryCatch(dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)), error = function(e) NA_character_)
  # 2) interactive fallback: current working directory.
  if (is.na(d) || !nzchar(d)) d <- getwd()
  # If we're in Codes/, the repo root is one up. Walk up until a repo marker shows.
  is_root <- function(p) dir.exists(file.path(p, "Data")) &&
                         dir.exists(file.path(p, "MINDSET_module-main"))
  cur <- normalizePath(d, winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE)
  for (i in 1:6) {
    if (is_root(cur)) return(cur)
    parent <- dirname(cur)
    if (identical(parent, cur)) break
    cur <- parent
  }
  stop("Could not locate the SSP-employment_estimates repo root from '", d,
       "'. Open this Rmd from inside the synced repo (its Codes/ folder).")
}
REPO <- find_repo_root()
cat("Repo root:", REPO, "\n")
MINDSET <- file.path(REPO, "MINDSET_module-main")

# ---- Scope (v1 = Morocco only; loop-ready) ---------------------------------
COUNTRY_ISO     <- "MAR"
COUNTRY_NAME    <- "Morocco"
COUNTRY_NAME_LC <- "morocco"   # region label as it appears in decomposed_ssp_output.csv

# ---- Inputs that EXIST (verified) ------------------------------------------
L_MATRIX_FILE   <- file.path(MINDSET, "SSP - Results", paste0("L_matrix_", COUNTRY_ISO, ".csv"))
L_DIRECT_FILE   <- file.path(MINDSET, "SSP - Results", paste0("L_matrix_direct_", COUNTRY_ISO, ".csv"))  # S25: direct-only jobs
CROSSWALK_FILE  <- file.path(REPO, "Data/Crosswalks/GLORIA-Eora26 - Crosswalk.xlsx")
PRODUCT_NUM_FILE<- file.path(REPO, "Data/SSP - Supporting Files/Gloria - Product list number.xlsx")
# CBA DOLLARS + line accounting. Both are produced by Codes/compute_cba_dollars.py,
# which replicates the SISEPUEDE CBA engine on decomposed_ssp_output.csv and reads
# the authoritative cb_config_params.xlsx (transformation_costs tab). That producer
# is the ONLY step that touches the separate ssp_morocco repo; it writes these two
# CSVs INSIDE this repo so the Rmd (what collaborators run) needs ssp_morocco NOT AT
# ALL. Re-run the producer whenever the CBA config or the decomposed run changes.
#   cba_dollars_by_line.csv : per (output_variable_name, time_period), FINAL signed
#                             $ (multiplier x delta x annual_change^t already applied).
#   cba_line_accounting.csv : all 55 config lines + disposition (live / visible_zero
#                             / excluded_config_bug / include_false / deferred_external)
#                             -> reproduces the silent-drop log with no ssp_morocco read.
DECOMP_FILE      <- file.path(REPO, "Data/CBA/sisepuede_results/sisepuede_results_sisepuede_run_2026-07-16/decomposed_ssp_output.csv")
CBA_DOLLARS_FILE <- file.path(REPO, "Data/CBA/cba_dollars_by_line.csv")
CBA_ACCT_FILE    <- file.path(REPO, "Data/CBA/cba_line_accounting.csv")

# ---- COST_MASTER: authoritative = NEW SSP CBA file (PENDING-1 RESOLVED) -----
# Some strategy columns here sum to <1 or 0 BY DESIGN: they are completed by the
# per-year electricity mix (S3) or by a source column, via the S2 supplement step.
COST_MASTER <- file.path(REPO, "Data/Cost Structure",
                         "Transformations - Cost Structure vectors (SSP CBA).xlsx")

# ---- REKEY crosswalk: CBA output_variable_name -> strategy_id (PENDING-2 RESOLVED)
# Built by Fernando; joins the authoritative cb_config_params.xlsx with zero misses.
REKEY_FILE <- file.path(REPO, "Data/Crosswalks/CBA_to_transformation_crosswalk_claude.csv")
REKEY_OVN_COL <- "output_variable_name"   # key on the CBA side
REKEY_ID_COL  <- "strategy_id_new"        # -> matches cost_struct$strategy_id

# ---- CBA run ids (from Session 7) ------------------------------------------
RUN_BAU      <- "72072"   # baseline
RUN_SCENARIO <- "73073"   # policy scenario

# ---- Output ----------------------------------------------------------------
OUT_DIR <- file.path(MINDSET, "GLORIA_template/Scenarios")
if (!dir.exists(OUT_DIR)) dir.create(OUT_DIR, recursive = TRUE)

# ---- Small helper: does a file exist? (used to skip pending sections) ------
have <- function(p) !is.na(p) && file.exists(p)

cat("File availability (all IN-REPO; ssp_morocco NOT required to run this Rmd):\n")
for (f in c(L_MATRIX_FILE, CROSSWALK_FILE, PRODUCT_NUM_FILE,
            CBA_DOLLARS_FILE, CBA_ACCT_FILE, COST_MASTER, REKEY_FILE)) {
  cat(sprintf("  [%s] %s\n", ifelse(have(f), "OK  ", "MISS"), f))
}
```

# S2. Cost structures (Eora26 sector x strategy)

**What this is.** For each transformation (strategy), a vector of weights over
Eora26 sectors that sums to 1: "of each dollar this transformation spends, what
fraction is bought from each sector." This is the object [PENDING-1] provides.

We read it into a tidy long table `cost_struct`:
`strategy_id | Sector (Eora26) | weight`, weights summing to 1 per strategy.

> IMPORTANT — DO NOT RENORMALIZE HERE. Some strategy columns in the master sum
> to <1 or exactly 0 BY DESIGN: they are completed by the per-year electricity
> mix (S3) or by a source column (e.g. Grid Upgrades, Industrial EE) in the S2b
> supplement step. Renormalizing now would erase the gap the supplement fills.
> Final renormalization happens ONCE, at the end of S2b, after supplementing.
>
> We therefore produce two objects here:
>   master_long   : the FULL long master (every column, incl. source columns like
>                   "Grid Upgrades") — needed by the S2b replace-with-source rule.
>   cost_struct0  : the raw numeric-id strategy columns only (may sum != 1).

```{r cost-structures}
if (have(COST_MASTER)) {
  sheets <- excel_sheets(COST_MASTER)
  read_one <- function(sh) { df <- read_excel(COST_MASTER, sheet = sh); df$.__sheet <- sh; df }
  raw_list <- lapply(sheets, read_one)

  # Each sheet: first column is the Eora26 Sector, the rest are value columns
  # (numeric strategy ids AND named source columns like "Coal", "Grid Upgrades").
  to_long <- function(df) {
    sector_col <- names(df)[1]
    df %>%
      rename(Sector = all_of(sector_col)) %>%
      select(-any_of(".__sheet")) %>%
      mutate(across(-Sector, as.numeric)) %>%
      pivot_longer(-Sector, names_to = "col", values_to = "weight") %>%
      mutate(weight = ifelse(is.na(weight), 0, weight))
  }
  master_long <- bind_rows(lapply(raw_list, to_long)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Sector)) %>%
    group_by(col, Sector) %>%                 # a column may appear on >1 sheet
    summarise(weight = sum(weight), .groups = "drop")

  # raw strategy structures = numeric-id columns only, NOT renormalized
  cost_struct0 <- master_long %>%
    filter(grepl("^[0-9]+$", col)) %>%
    rename(strategy_id = col)

  s0 <- cost_struct0 %>% group_by(strategy_id) %>% summarise(s = sum(weight), .groups = "drop")
  cat(sprintf("cost_struct0 (raw): %d strategies; %d sum to <0.999 (to be supplemented in S2b)\n",
              nrow(s0), sum(s0$s < 0.999)))
} else {
  master_long <- NULL; cost_struct0 <- NULL
  cat("[SKIP S2] COST_MASTER not found. Set COST_MASTER in S1.\n")
}
```

# S3. Dynamic electricity mix  [OPTIONAL — needs one wide CSV]

**Why.** When a transformation demands (or saves) *electricity*, the sectors it
hits depend on the grid mix. The old code froze this at the 2019 IEA mix. We
replace it with the SCENARIO's actual per-year generation by technology, so the
electricity portion of a cost structure tracks the decarbonising grid.

**Source.** `nemomod_entc_annual_production_by_technology_pp_*` columns inside
the wide `decomposed_ssp_output.csv` (run `RUN_SCENARIO`, region = Morocco).
That file has ~4,100 columns; base-R read segfaults on this machine
(see checkpoint). We therefore read only the columns we need, via a name filter.

> STATUS: this section is structured but LEFT INERT by default (`RUN_S3 <- FALSE`)
> because it feeds an enhancement, not the core jobs number. Turn it on once you
> and Fernando confirm the exact technology-column names and the source->Eora26
> generation-sector map (Session 7 rename map). The core pipeline (S4-S6) runs
> without it; electricity then falls back to whatever the cost structure carries.

This step RUNS BY DEFAULT now (`RUN_S3 <- TRUE`): the supplement in S2 needs it.
It builds `elec_by_year`: for each `time_period`, a vector of Eora26-sector
weights (summing to 1) = the year's generation mix applied to the per-source
cost structures on the `Synthetic_ind_energy` tab of COST_MASTER.

```{r dynamic-electricity}
RUN_S3 <- TRUE

# scenario technology token -> Synthetic_ind_energy source column (verified map)
tech2src <- c(coal="Coal", coal_ccs="Coal", gas="Oil and Gas", gas_ccs="Oil and Gas",
              oil="Oil and Gas", hydropower="Hydro", solar="Solar", wind="Wind",
              geothermal="Geothermal", nuclear="Nuclear", biomass="Bioenergy",
              biogas="Bioenergy")   # ocean, waste_incineration -> no target (dropped)

elec_by_year <- NULL   # filled below; consumed by S2
elec_avg     <- NULL   # year-averaged fallback (used if a period is missing)

if (RUN_S3 && have(DECOMP_FILE) && have(COST_MASTER)) {
  # --- per-source cost structures from the master's Synthetic_ind_energy tab ---
  sie <- read_excel(COST_MASTER, sheet = "Synthetic_ind_energy")
  names(sie)[1] <- "Sector"
  src_struct <- sie %>%
    pivot_longer(-Sector, names_to = "source", values_to = "w") %>%
    mutate(w = ifelse(is.na(w), 0, w)) %>%
    filter(source %in% unname(tech2src))     # keep generation sources only

  # --- per-year generation shares from the scenario run (73073) ----------------
  hdr <- names(read.csv(DECOMP_FILE, nrows = 0, check.names = FALSE))
  tech_cols <- grep("nemomod_entc_annual_production_by_technology_pp", hdr, value = TRUE)
  id_cols   <- intersect(c("primary_id", "region", "time_period"), hdr)
  gen <- read.csv(DECOMP_FILE, check.names = FALSE)[, c(id_cols, tech_cols)]
  gen <- gen[gen$region == COUNTRY_NAME_LC & gen$primary_id == as.integer(RUN_SCENARIO), ]

  # long: period x tech share -> map to source -> renormalize (after dropping unmatched)
  gen_by_src <- gen %>%
    select(time_period, all_of(tech_cols)) %>%
    pivot_longer(-time_period, names_to = "tech", values_to = "gen") %>%
    mutate(tech = sub(".*_pp_", "", tech)) %>%
    filter(tech %in% names(tech2src)) %>%
    mutate(source = tech2src[tech]) %>%
    group_by(time_period, source) %>% summarise(gen = sum(gen), .groups = "drop")

  # share = source generation / TOTAL generation THAT YEAR. Denominator computed
  # via an explicit per-year join (group_by %>% mutate proved unreliable here and
  # divided by the grand total across all years instead of the year's total).
  yr_total <- gen_by_src %>% group_by(time_period) %>%
    summarise(gen_tot = sum(gen), .groups = "drop")
  shares <- gen_by_src %>% left_join(yr_total, by = "time_period") %>%
    mutate(share = ifelse(gen_tot > 0, gen / gen_tot, 0)) %>%
    select(time_period, source, share)

  # per-year Eora26 electricity vector = sum_source share * source_struct
  elec_by_year <- shares %>%
    inner_join(src_struct, by = "source", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    group_by(time_period, Sector) %>%
    summarise(elec_w = sum(share * w), .groups = "drop")

  # year-averaged fallback (single vector) — mirrors the old static BAU_Electricity slot
  elec_avg <- elec_by_year %>% group_by(Sector) %>%
    summarise(elec_w = mean(elec_w), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(elec_w = elec_w / sum(elec_w))

  yr_sums <- elec_by_year %>% group_by(time_period) %>% summarise(s = sum(elec_w), .groups = "drop")
  cat(sprintf("[S3] elec_by_year: %d periods; per-year sum range [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
              nrow(yr_sums), min(yr_sums$s), max(yr_sums$s)))
} else {
  cat("[SKIP S3] needs DECOMP_FILE + COST_MASTER. Electricity supplement in S2 will be skipped.\n")
}
```

# S2b. Supplement + finalize cost structures (per year)

**Why this step exists.** Several strategy columns in the master are intentionally
incomplete; they are completed here per Fernando's supplement spec:

  - ELEC-ADD (`base + coef * Electricity`):
      3000 +0.12, 3010 +0.50, 3012 +0.10, 3018 +0.10, 3019 +0.44, 4000 +0.29
  - REPLACE with the whole electricity vector: 3013
  - REPLACE with a named source column: 3002 = "Grid Upgrades", 3008 = "Industrial EE"

Electricity is the **per-year** scenario mix from S3, so a supplemented strategy's
structure changes year to year (the grid decarbonises). Strategies not in the
spec pass through unchanged. Every strategy is renormalized to sum 1 at the end.
Output `cost_struct` carries a `time_period` column; non-supplemented strategies
are constant across periods (kept per-year for a uniform downstream join).

```{r cost-structures-finalize}
if (!is.null(cost_struct0)) {

  # --- supplement spec (from Fernando's code line; 0.44** read as 0.44*) -------
  # HOUSEKEEPING (Session 20, Fernando): three master columns were all-zero. Two are
  # completed here so the sum-to-1 invariant holds (they are NOT in the rekey -> no
  # CBA dollars route through them; this is report-readiness only, jobs unchanged):
  #   3005 = ENTC:TARGET_RENEWABLE_ELEC -> per-year grid-mix vector (replace_elec)
  #   3009 = INEN:INC_EFFICIENCY_PRODUCTION -> "Industrial EE" source column (replace_src)
  # The third, 3029, is the OLD-scheme id for 3013 (SCOE:SHIFT_FUEL_HEAT), already
  # built via replace_elec. It is a redundant empty duplicate -> left as-is (skipped).
  elec_add    <- c("3000"=0.12, "3010"=0.50, "3012"=0.10, "3018"=0.10, "3019"=0.44, "4000"=0.29)
  replace_elec<- c("3013", "3005")
  replace_src <- c("3002"="Grid Upgrades", "3008"="Industrial EE", "3009"="Industrial EE")

  # --- SAVINGS-SIDE ROUTING (Session 20) ---------------------------------------
  # 8 savings CBA lines were given NEW strategy_ids 8001-8008 in the rekey. Unlike
  # cost lines, a savings line is NOT a reuse of its cost twin's structure: the
  # money is spending DISPLACED from the fossil carrier the transformation stops
  # buying (S7/S13 displaced-carrier rule). So each 8000 id is CONSTRUCTED from a
  # displaced-carrier cost structure, exactly like `replace_src`, EXCEPT:
  #   - 8006 (INEN hi_heat) = 0.5*Oil and Gas + 0.5*Coal (high-heat industry burns
  #     both); a 50/50 blend, renormalized.
  #   - 8008 (ENTC opex) = the per-year grid mix (elec_vec), like `replace_elec`,
  #     because avoided grid electricity is displaced across the generation mix.
  # These ids have NO numeric column in the master (not in cost_struct0), so
  # build_one constructs them from the carrier structure and all_ids includes them.
  savings_src  <- c("8001"="Oil and Gas", "8002"="Oil and Gas", "8003"="Oil and Gas",
                    "8004"="Oil and Gas", "8005"="Oil and Gas", "8007"="Oil and Gas")
  savings_blend<- "8006"                 # 0.5 Oil and Gas + 0.5 Coal
  savings_elec <- "8008"                 # per-year grid mix
  savings_ids  <- c(names(savings_src), savings_blend, savings_elec)

  have_elec <- !is.null(elec_by_year)
  if (!have_elec)
    cat("[WARN S2b] No electricity vectors from S3; ELEC-ADD/REPLACE-ELEC strategies will be under-filled.\n")

  # periods to expand over (from S3; fallback to a single NA period if S3 inert)
  periods <- if (have_elec) sort(unique(elec_by_year$time_period)) else NA_integer_

  # numeric-id strategies from the master PLUS the 8000-block savings ids, which
  # have no master column and are constructed from displaced-carrier structures.
  all_ids <- sort(unique(c(cost_struct0$strategy_id, savings_ids)))

  # displaced-carrier structure lookup from the master (a named source column such
  # as "Oil and Gas" / "Coal", each summing to 1 on Synthetic_ind_energy).
  src_vec <- function(colname) {
    master_long %>% filter(col == colname) %>%
      group_by(Sector) %>% summarise(w = sum(weight), .groups = "drop")
  }

  # helper: electricity vector for a given period (per-year, else year-avg fallback)
  elec_vec <- function(tp) {
    if (!have_elec) return(tibble(Sector = character(), elec_w = numeric()))
    v <- elec_by_year %>% filter(time_period == tp)
    if (nrow(v) == 0) v <- elec_avg %>% mutate(time_period = tp)
    v %>% select(Sector, elec_w)
  }

  build_one <- function(id, tp) {
    base <- cost_struct0 %>% filter(strategy_id == id) %>% select(Sector, weight)
    if (id %in% names(elec_add)) {
      ev <- elec_vec(tp)
      out <- full_join(base, ev, by = "Sector") %>%
        mutate(weight = ifelse(is.na(weight), 0, weight),
               elec_w = ifelse(is.na(elec_w), 0, elec_w),
               w = weight + elec_add[[id]] * elec_w) %>% select(Sector, w)
    } else if (id %in% replace_elec) {
      out <- elec_vec(tp) %>% transmute(Sector, w = elec_w)
    } else if (id %in% names(replace_src)) {
      # source column lives in the FULL master (may be a non-generation column)
      out <- master_long %>% filter(col == replace_src[[id]]) %>%
        group_by(Sector) %>% summarise(w = sum(weight), .groups = "drop")
    } else if (id %in% names(savings_src)) {
      # savings displaced to a single fossil carrier (Oil and Gas)
      out <- src_vec(savings_src[[id]])
    } else if (id == savings_blend) {
      # 8006 INEN hi_heat: 0.5 Oil and Gas + 0.5 Coal (renormalized in the group step)
      out <- bind_rows(src_vec("Oil and Gas") %>% mutate(w = 0.5 * w),
                       src_vec("Coal")        %>% mutate(w = 0.5 * w)) %>%
        group_by(Sector) %>% summarise(w = sum(w), .groups = "drop")
    } else if (id == savings_elec) {
      # 8008 ENTC opex: displaced grid electricity -> per-year grid mix
      out <- elec_vec(tp) %>% transmute(Sector, w = elec_w)
    } else {
      out <- base %>% rename(w = weight)      # pass-through, unchanged
    }
    out %>% mutate(strategy_id = id, time_period = tp)
  }

  grid <- expand.grid(strategy_id = all_ids, time_period = periods,
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  cost_struct <- bind_rows(Map(build_one, grid$strategy_id, grid$time_period)) %>%
    group_by(strategy_id, time_period) %>%
    mutate(s = sum(w), weight = ifelse(s > 0, w / s, 0)) %>%   # renormalize ONCE, here
    ungroup() %>% select(strategy_id, time_period, Sector, weight)

  chk <- cost_struct %>% group_by(strategy_id, time_period) %>%
    summarise(s = sum(weight), .groups = "drop")
  nzero <- chk %>% filter(s < 1e-9) %>% distinct(strategy_id) %>% nrow()
  cat(sprintf("cost_struct (final): %d strategies x %d periods; sum!=1 (excl zero): %d; zero-structure: %d\n",
              n_distinct(cost_struct$strategy_id), length(periods),
              sum(chk$s > 1e-9 & abs(chk$s - 1) > 1e-6), nzero))
} else {
  cost_struct <- NULL
  cat("[SKIP S2b] cost_struct0 missing (S2 did not run).\n")
}
```

# S2c. Aggregate (`:all`) cost structures — REPORTING ROLLUP ONLY

**What this is.** Three CBA lines are aggregates over sub-components:

| `:all` line | component CBA lines | component strategy_id(s) |
|---|---|---|
| `inen:...:fuel_switch:all` | hi_heat, lo_heat | 3010, 3010 |
| `trns:...:efficiency:all` | electric, non_electric | 3015, 3015 |
| `ippu:...:abating_N2O_and_F_Gases:X` | n2o, other_fgases, pfcs | 4003, 4004, 4005 |

Their cost STRUCTURE is the **average of the component structures**, renormalized to
sum 1 (see [[cba-all-lines-not-aggregates]]). INEN and TRNS collapse to a single id
(both components share 3010 / 3015), so their aggregate IS that structure. Only IPPU
is a genuine mean of three distinct vectors.

> DOLLARS FLOW THROUGH COMPONENTS ONLY (Fernando, "Option 1"). The `:all` CBA line
> carries a DIFFERENT multiplier than its components; booking both the `:all` dollars
> and the component dollars would DOUBLE-COUNT the same spending. So these aggregate
> vectors are a **reporting rollup** — they are NOT rekeyed to a dollar-bearing
> strategy_id and NEVER enter the S4 dollar sum. The rekey leaves `:all` rows blank
> BY DESIGN; S4 logs that exclusion. This chunk exists only to let a subgroup's
> blended structure be inspected/reported alongside its components.

```{r aggregate-rollups}
if (!is.null(cost_struct)) {
  # component-id sets per aggregate (synthetic aggregate id -> its components)
  agg_map <- list("3010_all" = c("3010"),               # INEN fuel_switch:all
                  "3015_all" = c("3015"),               # TRNS efficiency:all
                  "4006"     = c("4003","4004","4005"))  # IPPU abating_N2O_and_F_Gases:all
  # 4006 = new synthetic id (next free in the 4000 block); *_all tags mark the
  # INEN/TRNS aggregates that are structurally identical to their single component.

  # WEIGHTING = SPENDING-WEIGHTED BLEND (Session 21, Fernando's choice).
  # The `:all` aggregate structure is the input mix of the COMBINED investment, so
  # each component's cost-structure vector enters weighted by its share of the
  # combined dollars (total |cba_dollars| over all periods -> one blend ratio per
  # component, applied every period). A zero-spend component therefore drops OUT of
  # the reported aggregate (e.g. 4004 IPPU:DEC_OTHER_FCS has $0 in this run: the 4006
  # blend becomes n2o ~58% / pfcs ~42% / other_fcs 0%, not the old 1/3-1/3-1/3 mean).
  # This SUPERSEDES the earlier simple-mean rule (see [[cba-all-lines-not-aggregates]]).
  # Single-component aggregates (3010_all, 3015_all) are unaffected (one component -> 1).
  # Fallback: if dollars are unavailable or all components net $0, revert to equal
  # weights so the sum-to-1 invariant can never break.
  comp_wt <- NULL
  if (have(CBA_DOLLARS_FILE) && have(REKEY_FILE)) {
    .dol <- read.csv(CBA_DOLLARS_FILE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    .rk  <- read.csv(REKEY_FILE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)[, c(REKEY_OVN_COL, REKEY_ID_COL)]
    names(.rk) <- c("output_variable_name", "strategy_id")
    .m <- merge(.dol, .rk, by = "output_variable_name")
    .m <- .m[!is.na(.m$strategy_id) & .m$strategy_id != "", ]
    .m$strategy_id <- as.character(as.integer(.m$strategy_id))
    comp_wt <- tapply(abs(.m$cba_dollars), .m$strategy_id, sum)   # total |$| per strategy
  }

  build_agg <- function(agg_id, comp_ids) {
    wt <- if (is.null(comp_wt)) setNames(rep(NA_real_, length(comp_ids)), comp_ids)
          else comp_wt[comp_ids]
    wt[is.na(wt)] <- 0
    if (sum(wt) == 0) wt <- setNames(rep(1, length(comp_ids)), comp_ids)  # equal-weight fallback
    wt <- wt / sum(wt)
    cost_struct %>% filter(strategy_id %in% comp_ids) %>%
      mutate(cw = wt[as.character(strategy_id)]) %>%
      group_by(time_period, Sector) %>%
      summarise(w = sum(weight * cw), .groups = "drop") %>%       # $-WEIGHTED blend of components
      group_by(time_period) %>%
      mutate(weight = if (sum(w) > 0) w / sum(w) else rep(0, n())) %>% ungroup() %>%  # renorm to 1 (guard /0 -> NaN)
      transmute(strategy_id = agg_id, time_period, Sector, weight)
  }
  agg_struct <- bind_rows(Map(build_agg, names(agg_map), agg_map))

  # INVARIANT: every aggregate sums to 1 per (id, period). See [[cost-structures-sum-to-one]].
  chk <- agg_struct %>% group_by(strategy_id, time_period) %>%
    summarise(s = sum(weight), .groups = "drop")
  if (any(abs(chk$s - 1) > 1e-6))
    stop("[S2c] an aggregate cost structure does not sum to 1 — build error.")
  cat(sprintf("[S2c] aggregate rollups built ($-weighted blend): %s ; all sum to 1 across %d periods.\n",
              paste(names(agg_map), collapse = ", "), n_distinct(agg_struct$time_period)))
  if (!is.null(comp_wt)) {
    w4 <- comp_wt[c("4003","4004","4005")]; w4[is.na(w4)] <- 0
    cat(sprintf("      4006 blend weights: n2o %.1f%% / other_fcs %.1f%% / pfcs %.1f%% (by |$| share).\n",
                100*w4["4003"]/sum(w4), 100*w4["4004"]/sum(w4), 100*w4["4005"]/sum(w4)))
  }
  cat("      (REPORTING ONLY — not rekeyed, not in the S4 dollar sum; components carry the $.)\n")
} else {
  agg_struct <- NULL
  cat("[SKIP S2c] cost_struct missing.\n")
}
```

# S4. CBA dollar scaling (signed cost and savings streams)

**The rule (Session 7).** Each CBA line is
`$ = multiplier x [ var(RUN_SCENARIO) - var(RUN_BAU) ]` per year — the multiplier
applies to the **delta** of the difference_variable, not its level.

**Sign at mapping (Session 19).** `cba_dollars` in the file is the ENGINE'S signed
figure; its sign encodes the physical DIRECTION of the delta (e.g. INEN energy use
FALLS under the scenario, so `technical_cost:efficiency` comes out negative), NOT
the economic role. For an employment demand vector we need the economic role:

  - `technical_cost`   -> POSITIVE demand (money spent -> orders placed -> jobs)
  - `technical_savings`/`consumer_savings`/`savings_opex`/`human_health`
                       -> NEGATIVE demand (displaced spending / avoided orders)

So we RE-SIGN each line to its economic role. We do NOT use `abs()`: that would
fabricate positive investment in the minority years where a line genuinely runs the
other way. Instead we orient each line by its OWN net direction and keep the
within-line flips:
`flip = target_sign(flow) * sign(sum_t cba_dollars_line)`, then `demand = flip * cba_dollars`.
Verified on the file: this makes all 30 cost lines net-positive and all 9
savings/other lines net-negative, while ~7 genuinely bidirectional lines (rail,
hdv, fgtv flaring/leaks/gas_recovery, INEN early-ramp, cons_ag, entc opex) retain
their opposite-direction years.

They are kept SEPARATE (different cost structures), then summed downstream:
net = cost + savings. We report gross(+), gross(-), and net side by side.
Savings are one-sided (no re-spending modeled) -> net jobs are a LOWER BOUND.

```{r cba-scaling}
# The dollars and the line accounting come from two IN-REPO CSVs produced by
# Codes/compute_cba_dollars.py (the only step that reads the separate ssp_morocco
# config). This Rmd therefore needs ssp_morocco NOT AT ALL.
#   cba_dollars_by_line.csv : per (output_variable_name, time_period), FINAL signed $
#       (multiplier x delta x annual_change^t ALREADY applied — we only JOIN, never
#        re-multiply). Formulas replicate the CBA engine; the engine is never run
#        (locked rule). Verified: INEN hi_heat total = -3.4767e9 (target -3.48e9).
#   cba_line_accounting.csv : all 55 config lines + disposition, so every excluded /
#       deferred / by-design-dropped line is logged (Fernando's silent-drop rule)
#       without reading cb_config_params.xlsx here.
if (have(CBA_DOLLARS_FILE) && have(CBA_ACCT_FILE)) {
  acct <- read.csv(CBA_ACCT_FILE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  # `cba` = the config lines the engine would BOOK (everything except include==FALSE),
  # mirroring the old `include==TRUE` filter. Classify flow by output_variable_name.
  cba <- acct %>%
    filter(disposition != "include_false") %>%
    mutate(
      flow = case_when(
        str_detect(output_variable_name, "technical_cost")    ~ "cost",
        str_detect(output_variable_name, "technical_savings") ~ "savings",
        TRUE                                                   ~ "other"
      ),
      subsector = str_split_fixed(output_variable_name, ":", 3)[, 2]
    )
  cat("CBA lines by flow type (config, include==TRUE):\n"); print(table(cba$flow))

  cba_dollars_tbl <- read.csv(CBA_DOLLARS_FILE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  # Join diagnostic BOTH ways so nothing drops silently (Fernando's rule).
  cfg_lines  <- unique(cba$output_variable_name)              # include==TRUE lines (54)
  csv_lines  <- unique(cba_dollars_tbl$output_variable_name)  # computed lines (42)
  orphan_csv <- setdiff(csv_lines, cfg_lines)                 # computed but not in config -> would drop $
  no_dollars <- setdiff(cfg_lines, csv_lines)                 # config line with no $ (deferred/excluded/gap)

  cba <- cba %>%
    left_join(cba_dollars_tbl, by = "output_variable_name")   # expands to per-period rows
  cba$delta <- NA_real_                                       # documented, unused (kept for schema clarity)

  # ---- SIGN AT MAPPING (Session 19) --------------------------------------------
  # `cba_dollars` carries the ENGINE sign (physical direction of the delta), which
  # is NOT the economic role. Re-sign to the role a demand vector needs:
  #   cost  -> +demand   |   savings / other benefit -> -demand.
  # NOT abs(): abs() would fabricate +investment in a line's minority-direction
  # years. Instead orient each line by its OWN net direction and keep within-line
  # flips: flip = target_sign(flow) * sign(sum_t cba_dollars); demand = flip*dollars.
  cba <- cba %>%
    group_by(output_variable_name) %>%
    mutate(
      target_sign = if_else(flow == "cost", 1, -1),           # savings & other -> -1
      .line_total = sum(cba_dollars, na.rm = TRUE),
      sign_flip   = target_sign * if_else(.line_total == 0 | is.na(.line_total),
                                          1, sign(.line_total)),
      demand      = sign_flip * cba_dollars                   # economically-signed $ for L %*% f
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(-.line_total)

  # Diagnostic: after re-signing, every cost line's net demand must be >= 0 and
  # every savings/other line's net <= 0 (the bug being fixed booked cost as -jobs).
  sign_chk <- cba %>%
    filter(!is.na(demand)) %>%
    group_by(output_variable_name, flow) %>%
    summarise(net_demand = sum(demand), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(ok = (flow == "cost"  & net_demand >= 0) |
                (flow != "cost"  & net_demand <= 0))
  n_flip <- cba %>% filter(!is.na(demand)) %>% group_by(output_variable_name) %>%
    summarise(has_flip = any(demand > 0) & any(demand < 0), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(has_flip) %>% nrow()
  cat(sprintf("[S4 sign] re-signed to economic role: %d/%d lines net-correct; %d lines keep within-line flips (not abs()).\n",
              sum(sign_chk$ok), nrow(sign_chk), n_flip))
  if (any(!sign_chk$ok)) {
    cat("[ERROR S4 sign] line(s) with wrong net demand direction after re-signing:\n")
    print(sign_chk %>% filter(!ok) %>% as.data.frame())
    stop("S4: sign-at-mapping produced a wrong-direction net demand.")
  }

  n_lines_live <- cba %>% filter(!is.na(cba_dollars)) %>% distinct(output_variable_name) %>% nrow()
  n_rows_live  <- sum(!is.na(cba$cba_dollars))
  cat(sprintf("\n[S4] Joined cba_dollars_by_line.csv: %d lines x periods -> %d rows with a $ figure.\n",
              n_lines_live, n_rows_live))
  cat(sprintf("[S4 join] %d include==TRUE lines | %d computed lines | %d orphan computed (must be 0) | %d config lines with no $.\n",
              length(cfg_lines), length(csv_lines), length(orphan_csv), length(no_dollars)))
  if (length(orphan_csv) > 0) {
    cat("[ERROR S4] computed lines absent from the config line set (silent loss of $):\n")
    print(orphan_csv)
    stop("S4: cba_dollars_by_line.csv has lines not present in cba_line_accounting.csv.")
  }
  # Log WHY each no-$ line has no dollars, straight from the accounting disposition.
  if (length(no_dollars) > 0) {
    cat("  [no $ figure — logged, NOT a silent drop]:\n")
    print(acct %>% filter(output_variable_name %in% no_dollars) %>%
            select(output_variable_name, disposition))
  }
} else {
  cba <- NULL
  cat("[SKIP S4] needs cba_dollars_by_line.csv + cba_line_accounting.csv",
      "(run Codes/compute_cba_dollars.py).\n")
}
```

```{r rekey}
# Re-key CBA output_variable_name -> strategy_id used by cost_struct (PENDING-2 done).
if (!is.null(cba) && have(REKEY_FILE)) {
  rekey <- read.csv(REKEY_FILE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    select(all_of(c(REKEY_OVN_COL, REKEY_ID_COL))) %>%
    rename(output_variable_name = all_of(REKEY_OVN_COL),
           strategy_id = all_of(REKEY_ID_COL)) %>%
    mutate(strategy_id = ifelse(is.na(strategy_id) | strategy_id == "", NA,
                                as.character(as.integer(strategy_id))))
  cba <- cba %>% left_join(rekey, by = "output_variable_name")

  # NOTE: `cba` is now per (line x time_period) after the S4 dollar join, so count
  # DISTINCT lines, not rows, or the tallies inflate ~33x.
  line_key <- cba %>% distinct(output_variable_name, strategy_id)
  matched   <- line_key %>% filter(!is.na(strategy_id)) %>% nrow()
  n_lines   <- nrow(line_key)
  unmatched <- line_key %>% filter(is.na(strategy_id)) %>% pull(output_variable_name)
  cat(sprintf("[S4 rekey] %d/%d CBA lines carry a strategy_id.\n", matched, n_lines))

  # The blank-strategy_id lines are NOT a silent drop — they are excluded on purpose,
  # for THREE distinct reasons. Log each bucket so the exclusion is documented, per
  # Fernando's silent-drop rule. (Categorised by output_variable_name token.)
  if (length(unmatched) > 0) {
    # mutually exclusive buckets (a savings-and-:all line is booked as savings first,
    # so each line is counted once): savings > :all > known-gap.
    is_savings <- grepl("technical_savings|consumer_savings|savings_opex|human_health", unmatched)
    is_all     <- grepl(":all$|abating_N2O_and_F_Gases", unmatched) & !is_savings   # aggregate rollups
    is_gap     <- !(is_all | is_savings)                              # known Session-3 gaps

    cat(sprintf("  [excluded on purpose] %d :all rollups | %d savings/externality | %d known-gap lines\n",
                sum(is_all), sum(is_savings), sum(is_gap)))
    # (a) :all aggregates: dollars flow through COMPONENTS only (Option 1). The
    #     aggregate STRUCTURE is built in S2c for reporting; summing :all $ on top
    #     of component $ would DOUBLE-COUNT (the :all line has a different multiplier).
    if (any(is_all)) { cat("   :all rollups (excluded from $ sum by design; see S2c):\n"); print(unmatched[is_all]) }
    # (b) savings / externality: resolve to a DIFFERENT object (displaced carrier /
    #     shadow price), not a strategy cost structure — savings side not yet wired.
    if (any(is_savings)) { cat("   savings / externality lines (routed elsewhere / not yet wired):\n"); print(unmatched[is_savings]) }
    # (c) known-gap lines with no rekey row (food waste x4, secondary forests, diets):
    if (any(is_gap)) { cat("   known-gap lines with no rekey mapping:\n"); print(unmatched[is_gap]) }
  }
} else {
  cat("[SKIP S4 rekey] needs cba (S4) + REKEY_FILE.\n")
}
```

# S5. Eora26 -> GLORIA (120 products)

Each Eora26 sector maps to one or more of the 120 GLORIA products. Following the
established convention, a sector's weight is **split evenly** across its GLORIA
products (no basis to favour one). Multi-sector products then sum. Result: a
120-product weight vector per strategy, still summing to 1.

```{r eora-to-gloria}
if (have(CROSSWALK_FILE) && have(PRODUCT_NUM_FILE) && !is.null(cost_struct)) {

  # Crosswalk sheet "Eora26 - GLORIA": rows = GLORIA products, cols = Eora26 sectors,
  # cell = 1 if linked. Pivot to long (Product, Sector) pairs.
  cw <- read_excel(CROSSWALK_FILE, sheet = "Eora26 - GLORIA")
  product_col <- names(cw)[1]
  cw_long <- cw %>%
    pivot_longer(-all_of(product_col), names_to = "Sector", values_to = "linked") %>%
    filter(linked == 1) %>%
    select(-linked) %>%
    rename(Product = all_of(product_col))

  # products per sector -> even split denominator
  ppc <- cw_long %>% count(Sector, name = "n_products")

  # GLORIA product code lookup (Lfd_Nr = the code MINDSET expects)
  prod_num <- read.xlsx(PRODUCT_NUM_FILE)   # cols: Lfd_Nr, Sector_names

  # NAME-DRIFT FIX: 3 product names in the crosswalk sheet differ from the
  # product-number file (verified 1:1 bijection -> pure naming drift, same
  # product). Without this, the name join below yields product_code=NA and the
  # product's demand silently vanishes from the 120-vector. Rename crosswalk
  # side -> product-number spelling before joining.
  gloria_name_fix <- c(
    "Glass and other ceramics n.e.c."                              = "Other ceramics n.e.c.",
    "Raising of sheep and goats"                                   = "Raising of sheep",
    "Repair and installation of machinery and equipment (service)" = "Repair and installation of machinery and equipment"
  )
  cw_long <- cw_long %>%
    mutate(Product = ifelse(Product %in% names(gloria_name_fix),
                            gloria_name_fix[Product], Product))

  # DATA CHECK: which Eora26 sectors carry weight but have NO GLORIA product?
  # Their weight would silently disappear in the join. Known cases in the OLD
  # master: "Wholesale Trade", "Retail Trade", "Re-export & Re-import" (trade
  # margins the crosswalk sheet does not map). Surface them so the leakage is a
  # documented choice, not a hidden bug. If any transformation puts real weight
  # on these, add crosswalk rows or reassign before trusting its jobs number.
  unmatched <- setdiff(unique(cost_struct$Sector), unique(cw_long$Sector))
  if (length(unmatched) > 0) {
    cat("[WARN S5] Eora26 sectors with no GLORIA product (weight will drop):\n")
    print(unmatched)
    leaked <- cost_struct %>% filter(Sector %in% unmatched, weight > 0) %>%
      group_by(strategy_id) %>% summarise(lost = sum(weight), .groups = "drop") %>%
      filter(lost > 1e-6)
    if (nrow(leaked) > 0) {
      cat("  Strategies losing weight to unmapped sectors:\n"); print(as.data.frame(leaked))
    } else {
      cat("  (No strategy puts weight on an unmapped sector -> no weight actually lost.)\n")
    }
  }

  # cost_struct is keyed by (strategy_id, time_period, Sector). Carry time_period
  # through so the GLORIA vectors stay per-year (electricity mix decarbonises).
  gloria_vectors <- cost_struct %>%
    # many-to-many is EXPECTED: one Eora26 sector -> several GLORIA products.
    left_join(cw_long, by = "Sector", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    left_join(ppc,     by = "Sector") %>%
    mutate(value_product = ifelse(is.na(n_products), 0, weight / n_products)) %>%
    group_by(strategy_id, time_period, Product) %>%
    summarise(value_product = sum(value_product), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(!is.na(Product)) %>%
    left_join(prod_num, by = c("Product" = "Sector_names")) %>%
    rename(product_code = Lfd_Nr)

  # ASSERT the name join lost nothing: any Product with NA product_code would
  # drop that product's demand silently. Print offenders and stop if any remain.
  na_code <- gloria_vectors %>% filter(is.na(product_code)) %>% distinct(Product)
  if (nrow(na_code) > 0) {
    cat("[ERROR S5] GLORIA products with no product_code (demand would drop):\n")
    print(na_code$Product)
    stop("S5: unmatched GLORIA product name(s) -> extend gloria_name_fix above.")
  }

  # Validation: each (strategy, year) GLORIA vector sums to ~1 (below 1 = weight
  # lost to unmapped sectors; 0 = strategy has no cost structure).
  chk <- gloria_vectors %>% group_by(strategy_id, time_period) %>%
    summarise(s = sum(value_product), .groups = "drop")
  cat(sprintf("GLORIA vectors: %d strategies x %d periods; weight-sum range [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
              n_distinct(gloria_vectors$strategy_id), n_distinct(gloria_vectors$time_period),
              min(chk$s), max(chk$s)))
} else {
  gloria_vectors <- NULL
  cat("[SKIP S5] needs crosswalk + product numbers + cost_struct (S2).\n")
}
```

# S6. Employment: jobs = L %*% f  (domestic only)

**The payoff step.** `L` is the 120x120 matrix built by `EXTRACT_L_MATRIX.py`:
`L[i, p]` = domestic jobs in product `i` per $1 of final demand booked to
product `p`. It already contains the Leontief inverse, employment coefficients,
and the import-origin split, and returns DOMESTIC jobs only. So once we have a
signed 120-product dollar vector `f` for a transformation, jobs are one
matrix product — MINDSET never runs again.

```{r load-L}
if (have(L_MATRIX_FILE)) {
  # row.names = output product code; columns = final-demand product code.
  L <- as.matrix(read.csv(L_MATRIX_FILE, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
  cat(sprintf("L loaded: %d x %d. Domestic jobs per $1 (col-sum) range [%.4g, %.4g]\n",
              nrow(L), ncol(L), min(colSums(L)), max(colSums(L))))
  # S25: direct-only requirements matrix (jobs to make the final-demand goods
  # themselves, no supply chain). Indirect = total - direct. Optional -> NULL if absent.
  if (have(L_DIRECT_FILE)) {
    L_direct <- as.matrix(read.csv(L_DIRECT_FILE, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
    if (!identical(dim(L_direct), dim(L))) {
      cat("[WARN] L_direct dims != L; ignoring direct split.\n"); L_direct <- NULL
    } else cat(sprintf("L_direct loaded: %d x %d (direct jobs per $1).\n",
                       nrow(L_direct), ncol(L_direct)))
  } else { L_direct <- NULL; cat("[note] L_direct absent -> total jobs only (no direct/indirect split).\n") }
} else {
  L <- NULL; L_direct <- NULL
  cat("[SKIP S6] L matrix not found. Run EXTRACT_L_MATRIX.py first.\n")
}
```

```{r jobs}
# LIVE: S4 dollars joined + S5 GLORIA vectors + L all present.
if (!is.null(L) && !is.null(cba) && exists("gloria_vectors") && !is.null(gloria_vectors)) {

  # 1) Dollars per (strategy_id, time_period, flow). Several CBA lines can share
  #    one strategy_id (INEN hi_heat + lo_heat -> 3010): they spend through the
  #    SAME cost structure, so SUM their dollars, then apply the structure once.
  #    (`:all` rollups already carry no strategy_id -> excluded here, no double-count.)
  #    Use `demand` (S4 economically-signed $: cost +, savings/other -), NOT the raw
  #    engine `cba_dollars` — otherwise cost lines that fall physically book as
  #    NEGATIVE jobs (the Session-18 sign bug).
  dol <- cba %>%
    filter(!is.na(strategy_id), !is.na(demand)) %>%
    group_by(strategy_id, time_period, flow) %>%
    summarise(dollars = sum(demand), .groups = "drop")

  cat(sprintf("[S6] $ groups: %d strategies x periods x flows -> %d (strategy,period,flow) cells.\n",
              n_distinct(dol$strategy_id), nrow(dol)))

  # 2) Book dollars onto GLORIA products via the per-year cost-structure shares.
  #    f_product = value_product (share, sums to ~1) x dollars, per group.
  # UNIT CONVERSION (critical): `cba_dollars` is in RAW DOLLARS, but MINDSET's L is
  # calibrated in THOUSANDS of dollars (L col-sums = domestic jobs per $1,000 of
  # final demand). So divide by 1000 before L %*% f, or jobs overcount 1000x.
  # (The old spine multiplied by 1000 for the opposite reason: its values were in
  #  $millions; $1M = 1000 thousand-$. Here we go raw-$ -> thousand-$, i.e. /1000.)
  USD_PER_L_UNIT <- 1000            # L is per $1,000 of final demand
  fdf <- gloria_vectors %>%
    inner_join(dol, by = c("strategy_id", "time_period")) %>%
    mutate(f = value_product * dollars / USD_PER_L_UNIT,    # -> thousands of $
           grp = paste(strategy_id, time_period, flow, sep = "|")) %>%
    group_by(grp, product_code) %>%
    summarise(f = sum(f), .groups = "drop")

  # 3) Assemble F (120 products x groups), rows ordered to match L's columns 1:120.
  Fmat_df <- fdf %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = grp, values_from = f, values_fill = 0)
  prod_order <- as.character(1:120)
  Fmat <- matrix(0, nrow = 120, ncol = ncol(Fmat_df) - 1,
                 dimnames = list(prod_order, setdiff(names(Fmat_df), "product_code")))
  rc <- as.character(Fmat_df$product_code)
  Fmat[rc, ] <- as.matrix(Fmat_df[, -1, drop = FALSE])

  # ALIGNMENT ASSERT: L columns must be product codes 1:120 in order, else the
  # matrix product silently mis-books demand. Stop rather than trust it.
  if (!identical(colnames(L), prod_order)) {
    stop("[S6] L column order != product codes 1:120 -> f/L misaligned.")
  }

  # 4) jobs = L %*% f, one column per (strategy, period, flow). Linear, so all at once.
  Jobs <- L %*% Fmat                     # 120 x groups, TOTAL domestic jobs by product
  grp_totals <- colSums(Jobs)            # total domestic jobs per group
  # S25: direct-only jobs (same f, direct requirements matrix). Indirect = total - direct.
  if (!is.null(L_direct)) {
    Jobs_direct <- L_direct %*% Fmat
    Jobs_indirect <- Jobs - Jobs_direct
  } else { Jobs_direct <- NULL; Jobs_indirect <- NULL }

  # 5) Tidy: split the group key back out and pivot flows to gross(+)/gross(-)/net.
  jobs_summary <- tibble::tibble(grp = names(grp_totals), jobs = grp_totals) %>%
    tidyr::separate(grp, into = c("strategy_id", "time_period", "flow"), sep = "\\|") %>%
    mutate(time_period = as.integer(time_period)) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = flow, values_from = jobs, values_fill = 0)
  # ensure both columns exist even if a flow is absent this run
  for (f in c("cost", "savings", "other")) if (!f %in% names(jobs_summary)) jobs_summary[[f]] <- 0
  jobs_summary <- jobs_summary %>%
    mutate(gross_cost = cost, gross_savings = savings + other,
           net = gross_cost + gross_savings) %>%
    select(strategy_id, time_period, gross_cost, gross_savings, net) %>%
    arrange(strategy_id, time_period)

  # jobs by product (120-vector) per group, kept for inspection / S7 export.
  jobs_by_product <- as.data.frame(Jobs) %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("product_code")

  # --- jobs by MINDSET (ISIC) sector over time, for the stacked chart (S24) -------
  # Jobs is 120 products x (strategy|period|flow). Map product 1..120 -> ISIC section
  # via the concordance tab (one-hot; row i = product i, cols A..T = 20 ISIC sections).
  conc <- readxl::read_excel(CROSSWALK_FILE, sheet = "GLORIA to ISIC concordance")
  isic_names <- as.character(unlist(conc[1, -1]))            # header row: section long names
  onehot <- as.matrix(conc[-1, -1]); onehot[is.na(onehot)] <- 0
  class(onehot) <- "numeric"                                 # 120 x 20 (product -> section)
  prod_to_sector <- isic_names[max.col(onehot, ties.method = "first")]  # length 120

  # Helper: melt a 120 x (strategy|period|flow) jobs matrix to long form, tagging the
  # ISIC sector, year, and the accounting flow (cost/savings/other). Reused for total,
  # direct, and indirect so all three share one shape. (S25)
  melt_jobs <- function(M) {
    as.data.frame(M) %>%
      tibble::rownames_to_column("product_code") %>%
      mutate(sector = prod_to_sector[as.integer(product_code)]) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(product_code, sector), names_to = "grp", values_to = "jobs") %>%
      tidyr::separate(grp, into = c("strategy_id", "time_period", "flow"), sep = "\\|") %>%
      mutate(year = 2015 + as.integer(time_period))
  }
  jobs_long_total <- melt_jobs(Jobs) %>% mutate(kind = "total")
  # net jobs (cost+savings) by sector-year -> the stacked chart input (unchanged).
  jobs_by_sector_time <- jobs_long_total %>%
    group_by(sector, year) %>% summarise(jobs = sum(jobs), .groups = "drop")

  # --- direct / indirect / total tidy long table (S25) --------------------------
  if (!is.null(Jobs_direct)) {
    jobs_long <- dplyr::bind_rows(
      jobs_long_total,
      melt_jobs(Jobs_direct)   %>% mutate(kind = "direct"),
      melt_jobs(Jobs_indirect) %>% mutate(kind = "indirect"))
  } else {
    jobs_long <- jobs_long_total
  }

  # --- investment flow by the SAME ISIC sector over time (S25) --------------------
  # The demand vector f that PRODUCED the jobs above, collapsed to the same sectors.
  # Lets us check feasibility: a big jobs bar should sit on a big investment bar;
  # large jobs off tiny investment => implausible labor intensity or mapping error.
  # Net final demand (cost + savings), matching the net-jobs construction. Fmat is in
  # thousands of $ (see USD_PER_L_UNIT above); x USD_PER_L_UNIT -> raw $.
  invest_by_sector_time <- as.data.frame(Fmat) %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("product_code") %>%
    mutate(sector = prod_to_sector[as.integer(product_code)]) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(product_code, sector), names_to = "grp", values_to = "f") %>%
    tidyr::separate(grp, into = c("strategy_id", "time_period", "flow"), sep = "\\|") %>%
    mutate(year = 2015 + as.integer(time_period)) %>%
    group_by(sector, year) %>%
    summarise(investment = sum(f) * USD_PER_L_UNIT, .groups = "drop")   # -> raw $

  # --- detailed jobs tables for export: direct/indirect/total (S25) --------------
  # (a) by LANDING sector x year (net over flows). Wide: one column per kind.
  # NOTE: `landing_sector` = the sector where the jobs ARE (the row of Jobs), NOT the
  # sector being invested in. So here "direct" means jobs in that sector from final
  # demand booked to that same sector; "indirect" means jobs pulled INTO that sector
  # as an upstream supplier to OTHER sectors' demand. A sector can therefore be ~100%
  # indirect (e.g. Trade, dragged in as a margin) or ~100% direct (e.g. Construction,
  # a final-demand target rarely used as an intermediate input) WITHOUT that saying
  # anything about that sector's own multiplier. For the "invest in X -> D+I jobs"
  # reading (own multiplier), use jobs_by_transformation_year_dit below instead.
  jobs_by_sector_year_dit <- jobs_long %>%
    group_by(landing_sector = sector, year, kind) %>%
    summarise(jobs = sum(jobs), .groups = "drop") %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = kind, values_from = jobs, values_fill = 0) %>%
    arrange(landing_sector, year)
  # (b) by transformation (investment target) x year (net over flows). THIS is the
  # policy reading: "invest in transformation X -> direct jobs (on the goods bought)
  # + indirect jobs (pulled through the Leontief inverse from all suppliers)".
  .cmap <- read.csv(REKEY_FILE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)[, c(REKEY_ID_COL, "strategy_code_new")]
  names(.cmap) <- c("strategy_id", "strategy_code")
  .cmap <- .cmap %>%
    mutate(strategy_id = ifelse(is.na(strategy_id) | strategy_id == "", NA,
                                as.character(as.integer(strategy_id)))) %>%
    filter(!is.na(strategy_id)) %>% distinct()
  jobs_by_transformation_year_dit <- jobs_long %>%
    group_by(strategy_id, year, kind) %>% summarise(jobs = sum(jobs), .groups = "drop") %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = kind, values_from = jobs, values_fill = 0) %>%
    left_join(.cmap, by = "strategy_id") %>%
    mutate(transformation = ifelse(is.na(strategy_code), strategy_id, strategy_code)) %>%
    select(strategy_id, transformation, year, dplyr::any_of(c("direct","indirect","total"))) %>%
    arrange(strategy_id, year)

  # (c) MECHANISM table (S26): jobs by landing_sector x transformation x year, split by
  # flow (cost = jobs-creating investment; savings/other = displaced spending). Lets us
  # explain each sector's TIME SHAPE by its driving transformations (traceability, Gap 1).
  jobs_mechanism <- jobs_long %>%
    filter(kind == "total") %>%
    mutate(stream = ifelse(flow == "cost", "investment_jobs", "displaced_jobs")) %>%
    group_by(landing_sector = sector, strategy_id, year, stream) %>%
    summarise(jobs = sum(jobs), .groups = "drop") %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = stream, values_from = jobs, values_fill = 0) %>%
    left_join(.cmap, by = "strategy_id") %>%
    mutate(transformation = ifelse(is.na(strategy_code), strategy_id, strategy_code),
           net = dplyr::coalesce(investment_jobs, 0) + dplyr::coalesce(displaced_jobs, 0)) %>%
    select(landing_sector, strategy_id, transformation, year,
           dplyr::any_of(c("investment_jobs","displaced_jobs")), net) %>%
    arrange(landing_sector, strategy_id, year)

  cat("[S6] Domestic jobs computed. Summary head (jobs are stock per the L units):\n")
  print(utils::head(jobs_summary, 8))
  cat(sprintf("[S6] net domestic jobs across all (strategy,period): %.1f\n", sum(jobs_summary$net)))
  cat("     (gross+ = cost-side demand; gross- = savings/displaced; net = sum. ",
      "Savings one-sided -> net is a LOWER BOUND on employment.)\n")
} else {
  jobs_summary <- NULL; jobs_by_product <- NULL
  cat("[SKIP S6] needs L + cba (S4) + gloria_vectors (S5).\n")
}
```

# S6b. Per-transformation cost: spreadsheet + charts (Fernando's request)

Reports the CBA dollar streams by transformation and year, in the SAME accounting
the jobs step uses: economically-signed `demand` (cost = +, savings/displaced = -),
grouped by `strategy_id` (several config lines share one — they spend through one
structure), and **excluding the `:all` rollups** (no strategy_id -> would double-count
against their components; this mirrors the S4/S6 exclusion). Scope = the job-routing
lines only (the transformations that reach the employment estimate), Fernando's call.

Products: (1) an XLSX + CSV by transformation x year with gross_cost / gross_savings
/ net; (2) the by-sector-and-year CSVs that feed the figures; (3) all five figures,
drawn by `Codes/CBA_figures.R` (sourced at the end of the chunk — see the note there).

```{r cost-by-transformation, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
if (!is.null(cba)) {

  # readable transformation label from the rekey strategy_code (falls back to id).
  code_map <- read.csv(REKEY_FILE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)[, c(REKEY_ID_COL, "strategy_code_new")]
  names(code_map) <- c("strategy_id", "strategy_code")
  code_map <- code_map %>%
    mutate(strategy_id = ifelse(is.na(strategy_id) | strategy_id == "", NA,
                                as.character(as.integer(strategy_id)))) %>%
    filter(!is.na(strategy_id)) %>% distinct()

  # by (strategy_id, year): sum economically-signed demand into cost / savings buckets.
  # Only job-routing lines (strategy_id present); demand already excludes NA-$ rows.
  cost_by_txn_year <- cba %>%
    filter(!is.na(strategy_id), !is.na(demand)) %>%
    mutate(bucket = ifelse(flow == "cost", "gross_cost", "gross_savings")) %>%
    group_by(strategy_id, time_period, bucket) %>%
    summarise(dollars = sum(demand), .groups = "drop") %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = bucket, values_from = dollars, values_fill = 0)
  for (b in c("gross_cost", "gross_savings"))
    if (!b %in% names(cost_by_txn_year)) cost_by_txn_year[[b]] <- 0
  cost_by_txn_year <- cost_by_txn_year %>%
    mutate(net = gross_cost + gross_savings,
           year = 2015 + as.integer(time_period)) %>%   # PERIOD_0 = 2015 (engine constant)
    left_join(code_map, by = "strategy_id") %>%
    mutate(transformation = ifelse(is.na(strategy_code), strategy_id, strategy_code)) %>%
    select(strategy_id, strategy_code = transformation, year, time_period,
           gross_cost, gross_savings, net) %>%
    arrange(strategy_id, year)

  # ---- EXPORT: xlsx (by-year sheet + totals sheet) + a CSV mirror ----------------
  txn_totals <- cost_by_txn_year %>%
    group_by(strategy_id, strategy_code) %>%
    summarise(gross_cost = sum(gross_cost), gross_savings = sum(gross_savings),
              net = sum(net), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(net)

  csv_out <- file.path(REPO, "Data", "CBA", "cost_by_transformation_year.csv")
  readr::write_csv(cost_by_txn_year, csv_out)
  xlsx_ok <- requireNamespace("openxlsx", quietly = TRUE)
  if (xlsx_ok) {
    openxlsx::write.xlsx(list(by_transformation_year = cost_by_txn_year,
                              transformation_totals  = txn_totals),
                         file = file.path(REPO, "Data", "CBA", "cost_by_transformation.xlsx"))
  }
  cat(sprintf("[S6b] exported cost_by_transformation_year.csv (%d rows)%s.\n",
              nrow(cost_by_txn_year),
              if (xlsx_ok) " + cost_by_transformation.xlsx (2 sheets)" else " (openxlsx absent -> CSV only)"))

  # ---- CSV exports that FEED the figures (S25) -----------------------------------
  # invest_by_sector_time = the demand vector f that produced the jobs, collapsed to
  # ISIC sections; jobs_by_sector_time = net jobs on the same sections. Written here
  # so the figure script below reads exactly what THIS run produced.
  if (exists("invest_by_sector_time"))
    readr::write_csv(invest_by_sector_time,
                     file.path(REPO, "Data", "CBA", "investment_by_sector_year.csv"))
  if (exists("jobs_by_sector_time"))
    readr::write_csv(jobs_by_sector_time,
                     file.path(REPO, "Data", "CBA", "jobs_by_sector_year.csv"))

  # ---- FIGURES: all five, drawn by Codes/CBA_figures.R (S27) ---------------------
  # The plotting code used to sit inline here. It now lives in ONE script so the
  # figures can also be re-cut on their own, without re-running this pipeline:
  #
  #     Rscript "Codes/CBA_figures.R"
  #
  # It reads only the three by-year CSVs written above plus the label crosswalks, and
  # carries the S27 chart brief (Fernando): x axis = PERIODS t_1..t_33 as plotmath
  # subscripts rather than calendar years (the paper reports periods and does not
  # stamp years onto the CBA ledger); savings ALWAYS BELOW ZERO, because the split is
  # now by the SIGN OF THE MONEY rather than by the line's cost/savings label -- the
  # CBA delta flips sign within a line, which is what put red bars above zero for
  # AGRC, ENTC and FGTV; and plain-language titles, sector names and measure names in
  # place of the SISEPUEDE codes. Sourced into its own environment so its ~40 helper
  # objects do not land in the pipeline's namespace; REPO is handed in explicitly so
  # the script uses THIS repo rather than re-deriving one from its own location.
  .fig_script <- file.path(REPO, "Codes", "CBA_figures.R")
  .fig_inputs <- file.path(REPO, "Data", "CBA",
                           c("cost_by_transformation_year.csv",
                             "investment_by_sector_year.csv",
                             "jobs_by_sector_year.csv"))
  if (file.exists(.fig_script) && all(file.exists(.fig_inputs))) {
    .fig_env <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
    assign("REPO", REPO, envir = .fig_env)
    source(.fig_script, local = .fig_env)
  } else {
    cat("[SKIP S6b figures] missing", if (!file.exists(.fig_script)) "Codes/CBA_figures.R",
        paste(basename(.fig_inputs[!file.exists(.fig_inputs)]), collapse = ", "), "\n")
  }

  # --- EXPORT: direct / indirect / total jobs spreadsheets (S25) -----------------
  if (exists("jobs_by_sector_year_dit")) {
    readr::write_csv(jobs_by_sector_year_dit,
                     file.path(REPO, "Data", "CBA", "jobs_direct_indirect_by_sector_year.csv"))
    readr::write_csv(jobs_by_transformation_year_dit,
                     file.path(REPO, "Data", "CBA", "jobs_direct_indirect_by_transformation_year.csv"))
    if (exists("jobs_mechanism"))
      readr::write_csv(jobs_mechanism,
                       file.path(REPO, "Data", "CBA", "jobs_mechanism_sector_transformation_year.csv"))
    if (requireNamespace("openxlsx", quietly = TRUE)) {
      openxlsx::write.xlsx(
        list(by_sector_year = jobs_by_sector_year_dit,
             by_transformation_year = jobs_by_transformation_year_dit),
        file = file.path(REPO, "Data", "CBA", "jobs_direct_indirect_total.xlsx"))
    }
    cat(sprintf("[S6b] direct/indirect/total jobs exported (sector & transformation x year) to %s.\n",
                file.path(REPO, "Data", "CBA")))
  }
} else {
  cat("[SKIP S6b] needs cba (S4).\n")
}
```

     against MINDSET's BATCH script, in the existing `Strategy_<id>_<ISO>.xlsx`
     "Investment by" format).
  2. The employment table (gross+/gross-/net by product and by strategy).
